items.title: Founded by a B.E. Engineer
items.description: Thiru. D. Ramprakash, son of M. Danapalan, established Ramanathapuram's first institution offering both hardware and software training — when personal computing was still a novelty in the district.

items.title: First internet in the district
items.description: Brought broadband connectivity to Ramanathapuram via a Chennai STD link, and conducted the region's first public internet awareness seminars, transforming access to digital knowledge.

items.title: Empowering the physically challenged
items.description: Ran a dedicated branch inside the Collectorate complex training differently-abled individuals as data entry operators and technicians — over 70% of BEL MNIC pilot operators were from this cohort.

items.title: Proprietorship registered
items.description: Formal registration of Computer Instruments on 1 December 1997 under Thiru. D. Ramprakash — establishing the commercial entity that still holds active AMC contracts with central and state government bodies.
